sentence: This project builds computer models of how lung cancer tumors and their surroundings change over space and time, using histology images.
This project studies the neural networks behind long-term memory problems in epilepsy and tests closed-loop ways to ease those problems.
This project provides gene and protein analysis, including DNA and RNA sequencing data, cell lines with edited genes, and protein studies by mass spectrometry.
This project builds ultrasound imaging methods and contrast agents to predict and follow the development of type 1 diabetes.
This project studies how the heart and vascular system work normally and abnormally, using bioinformatics and large biomedical data sets.
This project builds an online system that checks the radiation dose in a patient's daily anatomy and makes another plan for proton therapy when needed.
This project monitors antimicrobial resistance in bacteria found in meat, poultry and seafood sold in retail in Kansas.
This project tries to find groups of patients with pneumonia or sepsis who share features, so treatments can be matched to each group.
This project studies the molecular pathways that build and maintain the lens and builds a web tool that helps predict genes involved in cataracts.
This project tries to find human genes that matter for infection by viruses, by studying infection in a simple nematode and then in human cells.
This project tests whether single photon radionuclide imaging can be made far more sensitive and sharper than current clinical systems.
This project studies how proteins called visual pigments work in vertebrate vision and what goes wrong with them in retinopathies.
This project studies how genes in endothelial and smooth muscle cells raise or lower the risk of pulmonary arterial hypertension, using mice and human cells.
This project studies how arterial endothelial cells guide human pluripotent stem cells to become hematopoietic stem cells that can be transplanted.
This project studies how cells choose their fates during kidney development and disease.
This project builds computer modeling tools that help researchers understand how cells work and the cellular basis of disease.
This project builds computer tools that design drugs acting on the μ-opioid receptor to separate pain relief from dangerous side-effects.
This project studies the genetics of lymphoma in African Americans, who have worse outcomes than Caucasians.
This project studies how the breakdown of small RNAs called microRNAs shapes the making of blood cells, especially platelet-producing cells.
This project studies brain circuits involved in migraine pain.
